title: The problem of propranolol poisoning
authors: Williams H, Jagpal P, Sandilands E, Morrison E, Gray L, Thanacoody HKR, et al.
population: Patients whose intentional propranolol overdose requiring hospital attendance was reported to the UK National Poisons Information Service
funder: The authors state that they received no remuneration from any manufacturer or other company in connection with this study; no funder is named.
authorConflicts: The authors declare no conflicts of interest.
result: 444 enquiries concerned 363 intentional propranolol overdoses in 359 patients, 248 (69%) women, median age 32 years (interquartile range 22 to 45), 52 (14%) under 18. The indication was known in 121 cases and was anxiety in 111. In 43 of 61 cases with a co-prescribed antidepressant, both were taken. Outcome was confirmed in 159 exposures (44%): 110 recovered completely, 13 had ongoing features, one had permanent sequelae and 35 died. The authors advise primary care prescribers that propranolol for anxiety can be dangerous.
